results.question: Why does the author consider semantic caching's value more dubious than other caching techniques?
results.answer: The author considers semantic caching's value more dubious than other caching techniques because it is prone to failure due to its reliance on high-quality embeddings, functional vector search, and a reliable similarity metric. Additionally, determining the right similarity threshold can be challenging and may require extensive trial and error, leading to potential inaccuracies in returned responses. Furthermore, semantic caching can be time-consuming and compute-intensive, depending on the size of the cached embeddings.
